_note: The NODES-ALLOWED arm of kg-propose-edge. Third attempt at one question, and the two failures are recorded on DQ-T72 rather than discarded: c-kgedge-pending could not test approval at all (no approval), and c-kgedge-approved granted approval to kg_propose_edge, which the model never calls. This arm grants it to kg_add_nodes, the tool actually chosen, so the nodes can land and the follow-on becomes observable.

scenarios.prompt: Record that Aldric Vane and Mira Solene know each other.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['record that they know each other'] + ['link two characters'], grounded on the two seeded entities so the model has real names to resolve.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: TWO named entities, because the hard step is resolving NAMES to entity ids. With one entity the model cannot get the pair wrong and the scenario proves nothing about resolution.

scenarios.falsifier:
THE QUESTION: once the NODES are written, does the model go on to propose the EDGE the author asked for?

SUPPLIER-THEN-ACT (not a selection defect) IF kg_propose_edge is called after kg_add_nodes succeeds — the model was fetching a precondition, exactly as jobs_cancel -> jobs_list does.

A REAL SUBSTITUTION IF the nodes land and no edge is ever proposed: the author asked to record that two people know each other and got two nodes and silence.

🔴 NEITHER READING IS AVAILABLE IF THE NODES DO NOT LAND. Check that first — two arms have already failed on that exact point, one because the scenario auto-approved and one because the approval named the wrong tool.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A: the proposal must mint a review item, never a direct write.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an entity name that does not exist must be refused, not silently resolved to the nearest match.

scenarios._why_this_arm: 🔴 THE TOOL UNDER TEST IS DELIBERATELY THE ONE THE MODEL CHOOSES, NOT THE ONE THE PROMPT NEEDS — and that is the only difference from scenarios-c-blocked2.json. `--approvals allow-under-test` grants `allow` to exactly the batch's tools_under_test. With kg_propose_edge declared there, the approval landed on a tool the model never called, so all 5 runs of c-kgedge-approved still carded and nothing was written: the arm could not test what it was built to test. Naming kg_add_nodes here lets ITS write land, which is the precondition for the actual question.
